items.definition: The person who is in charge of you at work.
examples: My boss asked me to finish the report before lunch.
She is a very fair boss and always listens to the team.

items.definition: The money you receive every month for your job.
examples: The salary is good, but the hours are long.
He asked for a higher salary after two years in the company.

items.definition: A formal meeting where someone asks you questions to decide if you are right for a job.
examples: I have a job interview on Thursday morning.
She felt nervous before the interview but it went well.

items.definition: A person who buys goods or services from a shop or a company.
examples: The shop assistant helped a customer find the right size.
Our customers can pay by card or in cash.

items.definition: Working or studying for only some hours of the day or the week, not all of them.
examples: My sister has a part-time job at a café on Saturdays.
I work part-time so that I can look after my children.

items.definition: All the people who work for a company, a shop or a school.
examples: The staff at the hotel were friendly and helpful.
There is a meeting for all staff on Friday.

items.definition: A person who is paid to work for a company or another person.
examples: The company has more than two hundred employees.
Every new employee gets a short training course.

items.definition: A person who is in charge of a shop, a team or a department.
examples: The manager of the supermarket is looking for two new cashiers.
I need to speak to the manager about my holiday dates.

items.definition: An area of study at school or university, such as history or maths.
examples: Geography is my favourite subject because we study other countries.
How many subjects do you take this year?

items.definition: Work that a teacher asks students to do at home.
examples: I have a lot of homework to do this weekend.
Have you done your English homework yet?

items.definition: A written or spoken test of what you know.
examples: I have a maths exam tomorrow, so I am studying tonight.
She passed all her exams with good marks.

items.definition: A list that shows the times of lessons, trains or buses.
examples: My timetable is full on Mondays: I have six lessons.
Check the bus timetable before you leave.

items.definition: A qualification that you get when you finish a course at university.
examples: She has a degree in chemistry from Manchester.
My brother is studying for a degree in law.

items.definition: A child or young person who goes to school.
examples: There are thirty pupils in my daughter's class.
The teacher asked the pupils to open their books.

items.definition: A room in a school where a teacher gives lessons.
examples: The classroom was warm and the windows were open.
Please leave the classroom quietly when the bell rings.

items.definition: To not pass a test or an exam.
examples: He failed his driving test the first time.
If you do not study, you may fail the exam.

items.definition: The bags and suitcases you take with you on a journey.
examples: Our luggage was very heavy, so we took a taxi.
Can I leave my luggage at the hotel until the afternoon?

items.definition: An official document that you show when you travel to another country.
examples: I forgot my passport and could not board the plane.
Your passport must be valid for at least six months.

items.definition: The act of travelling from one place to another, especially a long way.
examples: The journey from Madrid to Paris takes about fourteen hours by car.
Have a safe journey and send me a message when you arrive.

items.definition: A short journey to a place and back, for example for pleasure or work.
examples: We are planning a weekend trip to the coast.
My boss is on a business trip in Germany this week.

items.definition: A journey in a plane, or a plane that makes a particular journey.
examples: Our flight to Dublin leaves at ten past seven.
It is a short flight, only about an hour.

items.definition: The raised area next to the railway line where you wait for a train.
examples: The train to York leaves from platform four.
We waited on the platform for twenty minutes.

items.definition: In or to a foreign country.
examples: She wants to study abroad for a year.
We usually go abroad in the summer.

items.definition: A person who visits a place for pleasure, not to live or work there.
examples: The old town is full of tourists in August.
A group of tourists asked me the way to the castle.

items.definition: A place where two or more roads meet.
examples: Turn left at the next junction and you will see the station.
There is often a traffic jam at this junction in the morning.

items.definition: A structure that carries a road, a path or a railway over a river or a road.
examples: We walked across the old stone bridge to the market.
The bridge is closed for repairs until next month.

items.definition: An open area in a town with buildings around it, often with cafés or a market.
examples: We had coffee in the main square and watched people go by.
There is a Christmas market in the square every December.

items.definition: Full of people.
examples: The metro was so crowded that I could not find a seat.
I do not like crowded beaches, so I go early in the morning.

items.definition: A person who is walking, not travelling in a vehicle.
examples: Drivers must stop for pedestrians at a crossing.
The city centre is now a pedestrian area, so there are no cars.

items.definition: A place by the road where a bus stops to pick up and drop off passengers.
examples: The bus stop is just opposite the post office.
I waited at the bus stop for half an hour in the rain.

items.definition: The building where the local government of a town or city works.
examples: You can get a copy of your birth certificate at the town hall.
The wedding photographs were taken in front of the town hall.

items.definition: To see or become aware of something.
examples: I did not notice the sign, so I took the wrong road.
Did you notice that the café on the corner has closed?

trap.en: Notice is a verb meaning to see something. The word for noticia is news (uncountable), never notice.
trap.es: Notice no es "noticia" (eso es news): notice es darse cuenta de algo.

items.definition: A piece of paper that shows you have paid for something.
examples: Keep the receipt in case you need to return the jumper.
The assistant gave me a receipt with my change.

items.definition: A lower price than the usual price.
examples: Students get a ten per cent discount in this shop.
There is a big discount on winter coats at the moment.

items.definition: A person whose job is to take payments from customers in a shop.
examples: The cashier scanned my shopping and told me the total.
She works as a cashier at the supermarket on weekends.

items.definition: A large basket on wheels that you push around a supermarket.
examples: I put the milk and the bread in the trolley and went to the till.
You need a pound coin to unlock a trolley.

items.definition: A line of people who are waiting for something, one behind the other.
examples: There was a long queue at the post office this morning.
In Britain, people usually wait in a queue and do not push.

items.definition: To put on a piece of clothing to see if it fits you and if you like it.
examples: Can I try on these shoes, please? I am not sure about the size.
She tried on three dresses before she chose the blue one.
collocations: a changing room to try on clothes

items.definition: Big in size or amount.
examples: I would like a large coffee and a small cake, please.
This jumper is too large for me; do you have a medium?

trap.en: Large means big, not long. For largo, say long.
trap.es: Large es "grande", no "largo". Largo se dice long.

items.definition: A pain in your head.
examples: I have a terrible headache and the bright light makes it worse.
Do you have anything for a headache?

items.definition: Something you take, such as a tablet or a liquid, to treat an illness.
examples: Take this medicine after meals, three times a day.
The pharmacist explained how to use the medicine.

items.definition: An illness or a reaction in your throat that makes you push air out noisily.
examples: I have had a dry cough all week and my throat hurts.
The cough kept me awake last night.

items.definition: A body temperature that is higher than normal because you are ill.
examples: She has a high fever and feels hot and shivery.
If the fever does not go down, call a doctor.

items.definition: A sports game between two teams or two players.
examples: We are playing a football match against the other school on Saturday.
Did you watch the tennis match last night?

items.definition: A place with equipment where people do exercise.
examples: I go to the gym three times a week after work.
She has a gym membership but she hardly ever uses it.

items.definition: Not ill, or good for your body.
examples: My grandfather is eighty, but he is still very healthy.
Try to eat a healthy breakfast with fruit and eggs.

items.definition: A person who lives next to you or very near you.
examples: Our neighbour waters our plants when we are on holiday.
I have never spoken to my neighbours in the flat upstairs.

items.definition: A ceremony in which two people get married.
examples: We are going to my cousin's wedding in July.
The wedding was in a small church by the sea.

items.definition: A child of your aunt or uncle.
examples: My cousin lives in Glasgow, so we only meet at Christmas.
I have six cousins, and we all get on well.

items.definition: To ask someone to come to a party, a meal or another event.
examples: She invited all her colleagues to her birthday party.
We invited our new neighbours to dinner on Saturday.

items.definition: Showing good manners and respect to other people.
examples: It is polite to say thank you when someone helps you.
The waiter was always polite, even when the restaurant was full.

items.definition: To feel sad because someone or something is not with you any more; also, to arrive too late for a bus, train or event.
examples: I miss my friends from the old school.
We ran to the station, but we missed the last train.

items.definition: To know that something or someone is there but to pay no attention to it or them.
examples: I sent her three messages, but she ignored them all.
He ignored the warning and walked across the road.

trap.en: Ignore means to pay no attention on purpose. It does not mean not to know something: for that, say not know.
trap.es: Ignore es hacer como si algo no existiera, no "ignorar" (no saber). Para no saber se dice not know.

items.definition: An event where musicians play or sing for an audience.
examples: We went to a concert in the park last Saturday.
The concert starts at eight, so let's meet at seven.

items.definition: A piece of paper or a code that lets you enter a place or travel.
examples: I bought two tickets for the cinema online.
You need a ticket to get into the museum.

items.definition: A long written story, usually about people who are not real.
examples: I am reading a novel about a family in the 1920s.
She wrote her first novel when she was twenty.

items.definition: An activity you enjoy doing in your free time.
examples: My hobby is photography, and I take pictures every weekend.
Cooking started as a hobby, but now it is my job.

items.definition: A picture that someone has made with paint.
examples: There is a beautiful painting of the sea above the sofa.
The museum has a famous painting by a Dutch artist.

items.definition: A series of public events, often music, films or food, that lasts for several days.
examples: We camped for three days at a music festival.
The town holds a film festival every September.

items.definition: A building where people go to watch plays; also plays as an art form.
examples: We booked seats at the theatre for Friday evening.
She studies theatre and wants to be an actor.
